BiblicalUsage: Ashkelon is a city of the Philistines on the coast, and it is named for Samson's vengeance, for David's lament and for the prophets' judgment. Samson goes down to Ashkelon and slays thirty men for their garments, David says tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon, Amos says God will cut off the inhabitant from Ashkelon, and Jeremiah says baldness is come upon Gaza, and Ashkelon is cut off.
TheologicalSignificance: A Philistine city named for a lament and for judgments tells me that Ashkelon is the place Israel's grief and God's judgment meet: David will not have Saul's death published in its streets, and the prophets say the city will be cut off all the same.
